items.evidence: Total, manual row amount and the reason title are asserted again after page.reload() (diff lines 132-147), so the test would fail if the mutation never ran.
Total after promotion less 25% (line 106), breakdown with manual 25% next to the line promotion (lines 115-128), and the total after a reload (line 134) are all asserted.
Reuses DraftOrderPage.create, addProduct, total, discountToggle, summary, dialog and statusInfo, and adds new members to DraftOrderPage. Nothing existing is duplicated.
No fixed waits. The method waits for the dialog to close and then relies on web-first assertions.
Imports test from fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.
Uses test ids, role-and-name locators scoped to summary or dialog, and listitem rows narrowed with anchored hasText filters. No CSS, XPath or positional selectors.
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO data. The draft is started with DraftOrderPage.create and the tee is added via addProduct, which is the suite's own pattern.
No ids. Every expected amount comes from PRODUCTS and PROMOTIONS in the orders scenario.
Uses the default admin actor through the fixture. No UI login and no credentials.
The type check exits 0 and the spec is at e2e/tests/orders/draft-manual-discount.spec.ts.

e2e/tests/orders/draft-manual-discount.spec.ts (diff lines 107, 117, 126, 138, 141): the spec writes the locator getByTitle("Discount amount") inline five times, chained on page-object locators, instead of putting a discount-amount locator on DraftOrderPage.
The new fields are readonly and built from this.page-derived locators. The existing constructor(readonly page: Page) {} is kept.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments, matching order-creation and draft-pricing.
One test, with a test.step for each stage.
The title states the behaviour and carries #e2e.
A header comment explains what the spec covers and why (diff lines 62-67).
All assertions are web-first (toHaveText, toContainText, toHaveAttribute).
Amounts are derived from scenario constants with guards and compared with toFixed(2). The scenario name is imported. The manual percent and reason are ticket data kept in a named constant.
No cleanup steps and no unique or random names.
No timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts, and test/expect come only from the fixture.
No any and no casts. The parameter objects are typed, and 'as const' on a literal is not a type-loosening cast.
The comments explain reasons (toggle state, dialog closing on error, identical amounts needing scoped rows) rather than narrating the next line.

structured_output.summary: A strong submission. It extends DraftOrderPage with scoped readonly locators and an addOrderDiscount method, works out every expected value from the scenario constants with guards, and proves the discount was saved by reading the total, the breakdown and the reason again after a reload. The type check passes. The only finding is a minor M1: the spec repeats the getByTitle("Discount amount") locator inline instead of defining it on the page object.
